	if len(parts) != 4:
		# A date that has not arrived yet leaves the expression short. The

		# is the honest answer - and an empty result renders, where an
		# exception renders as a red box over the chart.
		return None
	line_name = parts[0]

		return None
	start_time = system.date.fromMillis(long(parts[2]))
	if not parts[3].isdigit():
		return None
	stop_time = system.date.fromMillis(long(parts[3]))
	return launchpad.store.rowsAsJson(launchpad.store.hourlyStatsAverage(line_name, tag_folder, start_time, stop_time))

pyData = system.dataset.toPyDataSet(value.data)
	headers = ["Timestamp", "Availability", "Performance", "Quality", "OEE"]
	data = []
	# The last row is the interval currently in progress, and plotting a part-
	# finished hour drags the line down for no real reason -- so drop it, but
	# ONLY in Realtime. In Historical mode every row is a completed interval
	# and the last one belongs on the chart, so the mode has to be read from
	# the session (view.custom.timeRange is not a property of this view).
	rows = pyData.getRowCount()
	if value.mode == 'Realtime' and rows > 0:
		rows -= 1
	for r in range(rows):
		data.append([pyData.getValueAt(r, "time_stamp"), pyData.getValueAt(r, "oee_a"),
		             pyData.getValueAt(r, "oee_p"), pyData.getValueAt(r, "oee_q"),
		             pyData.getValueAt(r, "oee")])
	return system.dataset.toDataSet(headers, data)
